class: A gate that runs its seconds-long checks after its minutes-long stages reports the cheap red only after the whole wait, so every cheap failure costs a full gate run; the cheap checks must run first.
mechanism: scripts/orchestrator/prepush.py ordered frontend_build, preflight, ci_checks, domain_tests, app_tests, then ruff_ratchet, coverage, alembic_guard, frontend_lint last. A ratchet or lint failure was therefore found only after the long stages had finished, and the whole gate was run again.

first_seen.evidence: Measured: 2007 s total; ruff_ratchet 0.6 s, coverage 1.3 s, alembic_guard 0.2 s and frontend_lint 8 s ran after ~1985 s of long stages; 12 gate runs failed late and were re-run in full.

fix: prepush.py runs ruff_ratchet, coverage, alembic_guard, frontend_lint and frontend_build first, then preflight, ci_checks, domain_tests, app_tests, frontend_unit. Every step still runs after a red one, except that a red preflight stops the run. tests/orchestrator/test_prepush.py pins the order and that a red cheap check still lets preflight and every later step run.

detection.note: The order test fails if a cheap step moves behind a long one.

occurrences.evidence: 12 gate runs failed late on a cheap check and were re-run in full (2007 s total per run; the cheap checks need about 10 s).
